description: The portfolio's configuration is extended by name rather than copied: what belongs to ten repositories lives in `youndie/sborka`, and what is here is what only this repository can decide.

`automerge-harness` is extended second, and its precondition was checked rather than assumed. It is only safe where a pull request actually runs the build — and both workflows here do, on `pull_request`, verified by watching them run rather than by reading their triggers. Neither had ever executed before 2026-09-16: `build.yaml` did not parse, and `check.yaml` had no JDK. A green-looking pull request in that state means nobody ran anything, which is exactly the counter-example the harness preset names.
The order matters: package rules are concatenated preset-first and the last match wins, so the harness rule has to come after the base preset's 'a major gets a human'.

chronik is one release across three modules, and taking them apart is a link error rather than a version skew. `chronik-core` carries the contract, `chronik-sqlx4k-sqlite` the store that implements it and `chronik-conformance` the corpus that decides whether a store is correct — a repository holding one version of the corpus against another of the store is asking a different question from the one it thinks it is asking.
The same shape as the preset's `sborka` rule and for the same reason: one number in the catalogue, one pull request.

sqlx4k moves with chronik whether or not Renovate knows it. `chronik-sqlx4k-sqlite` is compiled against a particular sqlx4k, and this repository pins the same number for its own SQLite driver: 1.13.0 against 1.13.1 was found by reading chronik's POM, not by a failure, and the failure it would have produced is a link error rather than a resolution one.
They are grouped so the build checks them together. They are NOT pinned to each other, because they release independently and a rule that pretended otherwise would hold back whichever moved first.

kore is two libraries and a Gradle plugin that generates the object those libraries read. A plugin from one version with a library from another compiles and then disagrees about the shape of `KoreBuildIdentity` — the catalogue says so where the version is declared, and this keeps the bump honouring it.
This repository's own image is not a dependency of itself. Renovate offering a bump of `ghcr.io/youndie/xyk` would be offering the tag this repository publishes.

THE GENERATOR'S IMAGE IS PINNED IN SHELL, WHERE THE DOCKER MANAGER CANNOT SEE IT. `K6_IMAGE=${K6_IMAGE:-grafana/k6:0.54.0}` appears in four harnesses under `bench/`, and a bumper that sees one form of a pin and not another leaves the unseen one behind for ever — which is worse than not bumping at all, because the repository then has two versions of the same tool and one of them is invisible.
It is a `customType: regex` rather than a refactor into a single file because the harnesses are meant to be runnable one at a time, by hand, without sourcing anything.

`managerFilePatterns` rather than `fileMatch`: the running app is Renovate 44, where the older name is gone. Validated against 44 — an older validator accepts only the old name and would have passed a config the app then ignores, which is a manager that manages nothing and says so nowhere.
